Former Portuguese Jewish Community Synagogue in Hamburg

Former Synagogue · Hamburg, Germany

Hamburg's Portuguese Jewish community rented and remodelled the residential building at Innocentiastraße 37 in 1935 for use as a synagogue by its approximately 150 members. The Sephardic congregation held services there until the end of 1939. From 1941, Nazi authorities used the building as a so-called Judenhaus and assembly point connected with forced relocation and deportation. The structure survives, but it no longer functions as a synagogue and has returned to residential use. Its surviving inscription recalls the former Sephardic congregation Bet Israel.
